title.en: The Nuclear Question: Taiwan's Energy Trilemma
The Day the Reactor Went Quiet

A2.text: On May 17, 2025, Taiwan turned off its last nuclear reactor. Just three months later, voters were asked to turn it back on completely. So what really changed?
A2.authored_by: Claude (Gemini draft unavailable due to API quota; hand-authored to the same standard)
A2.basis: New mission, no workbook source. Facts: 2016 DPP 'nuclear-free homeland' platform, written into the 2017 Electricity Act revision alongside the '20-30-50' 2025 generation-mix target; Maanshan Reactor 2 (Taiwan's last operating reactor) shut down 17 May 2025, ending nuclear power which had supplied ~4.2% of 2024 generation (288 TWh total, of which 42.4% gas / 39.3% coal / 11.6% renewables); 23 August 2025 referendum (Proposal No. 21) on restarting Maanshan: 74.2% yes among ~5.8M votes cast (~4.3M yes vs ~1.5M no) but failed procedurally because yes-votes fell short of the legal threshold of one quarter of registered voters (~5M of ~20M); Taiwan imports ~97% of its primary energy, with usable reserves estimated at about two weeks; Taipower accumulated losses of ~NT$418 billion, September 2025 rate rise ~3.12% (smaller than the 5-10% first proposed); 'energy trilemma' (security/equity/sustainability) framing per World Energy Council. Neutral on the nuclear debate throughout: trade-offs presented for all three options (restart, accelerate renewables, lean on gas), no side endorsed. Register per docs/plans/new-mission-playbook.md. Authored by Claude directly (Gemini 3.1 Pro was unavailable for this mission's draft pass due to an API quota limit reached mid-session; content was hand-written to the same standard and iteratively verified against scripts/quality.py and scripts/grammar_range.py).
